headline: St. Lucie County Firefighter-Paramedic Austin Hodge Dies in Line of Duty
teaser: St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge died while on duty Oct. 24, about 15 months after his brother Jarius, also a firefighter. The district and fellow first responders are mourning his death.
body:
ST. LUCIE COUNTY — Firefighter-Paramedic Austin Hodge died Saturday, Oct. 24, while on duty, the St. Lucie County Fire District announced.

Hodge joined the district on July 17, 2017, and served the community for more than nine years. He was assigned to Station 9.

His death came about 15 months after the loss of his younger brother, Jarius Hodge, who also served as a firefighter-paramedic with the district. Jarius became ill while working at Station 3 in July 2025 and later died at a hospital. The brothers shared a commitment to firefighting and served the same community.

After Jarius died, Austin spoke publicly about their close relationship. “He was my best friend,” he said at the time. “Talked to him every day.”

At a family gathering on May 30, 2026, marking what would have been Jarius’s 27th birthday, Austin reflected on his younger brother’s influence. “He was my younger brother, but I looked up to him in many ways to keep me poised, keep me patient,” he said.

On Saturday, firefighters and public safety personnel escorted Austin Hodge in a procession from the hospital to the morgue in Fort Pierce. The Fire District thanked the St. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office, Fort Pierce Police Department, Port St. Lucie Police Department, and peer support teams from Martin and Indian River counties for helping its members honor him.

In a public message following Austin’s death, the district emphasized the support shown by first responders across the region. “The brotherhood of the fire service extends far beyond the walls of a fire station,” the district wrote. It also thanked community members for their condolences and assistance.

The district called Austin’s death “a profound loss” to its members and the wider fire service community and extended condolences to his family, friends and fellow firefighters. Its October 24 announcement did not disclose the circumstances of his death.

The Fire District asked that Austin’s family be given privacy as they grieve. Memorial arrangements and opportunities to honor his service will be announced in coordination with his family as details are finalized.
